source: YouTube auto-caption transcript 0:00-15:45 (tools/video_draft.py transcript GRW7THxCZuk --start 0 --end 945); nothing past 15:45 read. 'type' marks each idea as claim, heuristic or one-off pick; 'repeats' lists ideas of earlier videos it restates; 'related' lists looser topic matches. Solo draft: every idea is the host's (speaker field kept for the schema).

ideas.speaker: Paul Cheon (host)
ideas.claim: Violent Echoes is a really good uncommon: it usually kills something and draws a card for four mana; it is the pick over a rare (Samut) in a weak pack.
ideas.quote: Most of the time, you're going to kill something and then draw a card, right? Which is excellent for a four-mana spell.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Violent Echoes against Samut, Hazoret's Champion.

ideas.speaker: Paul Cheon (host)
ideas.claim: Verdant Kraken is a legitimate bomb that you must build around (ramp); he takes it over solid red removal (No Admittance) and a second pick of the first colour.
ideas.quote: This card is a legitimate bomb. You just have to build around it.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Verdant Kraken, and of decks with 2+ ramp cards.

ideas.speaker: Paul Cheon (host)
ideas.claim: Protege's Awakening is the better card than Way of the Wildspeaker and is perfectly splashable.
ideas.quote: Protege's Awakening is a better card ... it's also a perfectly fine splashable
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Protege's Awakening as a splash.

ideas.speaker: Paul Cheon (host)
ideas.claim: Take the best card each pick and let colours come later: Primal Witchstalker is best in the pack at P1p4 even though he may end up Sultai and abandon red.
ideas.quote: We're just taking it one pick at a time. I'm just taking the best card.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Primal Witchstalker by pick number.

ideas.speaker: Paul Cheon (host)
ideas.claim: Pick the graveyard-value card (Something Worth Saving) over a big top-end (Archive Arbiter) because large creatures are easier to find later than value cards.
ideas.quote: I think I'm more likely to be able to just find random large creatures to put into my deck.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Something Worth Saving against Archive Arbiter.

ideas.speaker: Paul Cheon (host)
ideas.claim: Vinelasher Adept (basic landcycling) smooths draws and keeps the second colour open; it also makes splashing a busted card like Aerid Konstrari possible.
ideas.quote: I think I'm going to take Vine Lasher Adept because it smooths out your draws
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Vinelasher Adept; splash success of decks that play it.

ideas.speaker: Paul Cheon (host)
ideas.claim: In a weak pack with nothing to play, take the splash land (Fatehold Annex) because it is the card he will actually use.
ideas.quote: I don't really want to play any of these cards. ... That is a card that I'm looking to splash.
ideas.test_idea: Playable-count threshold below which a dual land beats the best filler.

ideas.speaker: Paul Cheon (host)
ideas.claim: Take cheap interaction (Last Gasp) over a very strong card (Plan for All Outcomes) because decks like this are clunky and a cheap trick shores up their weak turns.
ideas.quote: often times when I draft these decks, I find that they can be a little clunky and Last Gasp really helps shore up a lot of things.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Last Gasp in ramp / self-mill decks.

ideas.speaker: Paul Cheon (host)
ideas.claim: Aerid Konstrari (a 5/4 flyer that leaves a Heartwood token) is worth splashing; that is the reason to take the landcycler earlier.
ideas.quote: this is why you take the Vine Lasher Adept, right? Because it gives you the opportunity to splash for busted cards like the Aerid Konstrari.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Aerid Konstrari when splashed.

ideas.speaker: Paul Cheon (host)
ideas.claim: Recursive Recruitment is a premium uncommon in self-mill decks and justifies moving towards four colours, at the price of having to respect the mana.
ideas.quote: recursive recruitment seems awesome in this style of deck ... now I'm going to need to respect my mana to some degree
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Recursive Recruitment by mill-card count.

ideas.speaker: Paul Cheon (host)
ideas.claim: Murmuring Volume over Theoretical Necromancer: it lets the deck cast all its cards (fixing plus card draw) and suits self-mill and ramp.
ideas.quote: This lets us just cast all of our cards
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Murmuring Volume in 3+ colour decks.

ideas.speaker: Paul Cheon (host)
ideas.claim: Take the solid cheap creature (Arcane Amphisbaena: deathtouch plus surveil) in a deck that already has plenty of expensive cards.
ideas.quote: I don't need good expensive cards like the Archive Arbiter. I will very happily take the Arcane Amphisbaena here as a solid two-drop.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Arcane Amphisbaena against Archive Arbiter.

ideas.speaker: Paul Cheon (host)
ideas.claim: Commit to full ramp with several colours (green-black base splashing blue and red) and take the second Murmuring Volume over weaker playables.
ideas.quote: Let's go full ramp. ... Green black base splashing blue and red
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of four-colour ramp decks with 2+ Murmuring Volume.

ideas.speaker: Paul Cheon (host)
ideas.claim: Cheap ramp creatures (Konstrari Improviser) are worth taking as extra ways to reach the Verdant Kraken.
ideas.quote: solid two-drop that helps me ramp. Just more ways to try to get to that Verdant Kraken is nice.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Konstrari Improviser in decks with Verdant Kraken.

ideas.speaker: Paul Cheon (host)
ideas.claim: Pick up dual lands once splash cards are held, taking the land over a playable (Way of the Wildspeaker).
ideas.quote: at this point I would like to be able to pick up some lands to be able to support some of these cards
ideas.test_idea: Playable-count threshold below which a dual land beats the best filler.

ideas.speaker: Paul Cheon (host)
ideas.claim: He does not main-deck Essence Burn and wonders whether to hate-draft it; pick 11 is spent on a card he will not play.
ideas.quote: I'm not main decking Essence Burn. ... Like I wonder if hate drafting even
ideas.test_idea: Hate-draft value of late narrow removal.

ideas.speaker: Paul Cheon (host)
ideas.claim: Double blue is really hard in a deck that only splashes blue; he passes Mind Meanderer for a worse card and takes it later when it wheels.
ideas.quote: double blue is really hard, right? So, I don't think I take it here.
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Mind Meanderer by blue source count.

ideas.speaker: Paul Cheon (host)
ideas.claim: A dual land (Innovative Commons, then Formidable Commons earlier at P3p4) is taken over a marginal playable when the deck is a ramp deck casting everything.
ideas.quote: I'll take a blue red land with nothing else available.
ideas.test_idea: Dual land against the best filler by number of splash cards held.

ideas.speaker: Paul Cheon (host)
ideas.claim: Protege's Awakening and Arni are playable in the deck for card draw if the mana allows.
ideas.quote: I can probably play Protege's Awakening for like a little more card draw
ideas.test_idea: GIH WR of Protege's Awakening in 3+ colour decks.

ideas.speaker: Paul Cheon (host)
ideas.claim: With little interaction and a deck that needs a late game, go full three-colour (Sultai) and play more Islands, relying on four dual lands.
ideas.quote: I think we're just going to go full Sultai and just play a lot more Islands.
ideas.test_idea: WR of Sultai ramp decks against two-colour decks with a splash.

ideas.speaker: Paul Cheon (host)
ideas.claim: His creature count is absurdly high and the deck has not one way to recur; he cuts Hapatra, which does not do much, and one Sureshot Sower.
ideas.quote: Our creature count's absurdly high.
ideas.test_idea: Creature-count ceiling in the deck model.

ideas.speaker: Paul Cheon (host)
ideas.claim: He does not want 16 lands in a mana-heavy deck of this type and plays 17.
ideas.quote: Very, very heavy on mana, but I don't think I want to play 16 lands with this type of deck.
ideas.test_idea: WR of 16 against 17 lands in three-colour ramp decks.

ideas.speaker: Paul Cheon (host)
ideas.claim: Count blue sources including non-land fixers: two Islands plus the dual lands and the two Murmuring Volumes is enough (five blue sources plus the Volumes) for Mind Meanderer and the blue cards.
ideas.quote: That still gives me five blue sources plus the two Murmuring Volumes, so yeah, we'll cut a swamp.
ideas.test_idea: Source counts including Murmuring Volume against play rate.
